Update, taking @TokageItLab's concerns into account along with some of my own considerations.

Firstly, it felt problematic to treat almost every incremental step of the construction of an AnimationTree as a mistake to be pointed out to the user, since they are all necessary to arrive at a solution... unless their visibility can be tightly scoped - like they are to the currently open script in Script Editor. Similarly, the user should not be pestered about things they may have left error-worthy on purpose. So, a toast was out of the question. Instead, the error bar is now almost exactly like the Script Editor's, with a few caveats.

Firstly, only 1 active error from the current node's scope is always shown in the left. However, this error may only appear if it affects the currently open node, not its parents or children, so that instructions to fix things are only forced onto the user when they are actually relevant. Clicking it will take you to* that error, which is only a meaningful interaction for BlendTree right now, but that same flash&pan can be added for others too, in the future.

Secondly, the errors that now appear when navigating into nodes create general awareness for the red button on the right, which still keeps a tally of ALL active errors in the AnimationTree, and can be clicked to browse them, entirely analogue to Script Editor's.

Thirdly, to have consistent behavior across all types of nodes, `meta_clicked` now takes you _inside_* the affected node, rather than to its parent, which it was only previously doing for BlendTree. So, now, when you see an error like "No blend points exist, so blending cannot take place", you're taken into the specific BlendSpace1D owning that error, rather than to its parent StateMachine, which might have many BlendSpace1D's that are all affected by this.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c263230-5a1b-4775-932d-ecdeabea30f3

In my opinion, what the error scope indicates isn’t important, but rather that users should be able to determine why the AnimationTree isn’t working. After all, if the AnimationTree won’t work unless all errors are resolved, I believe that error message should appear at least one line somewhere.

Consequently, I don’t see much point in distinguishing whether an error is nested or not. If a click-to-navigate feature is added, these errors should certainly be treated in parallel. As I mentioned above, if it can be guaranteed that at least one line of error text will always be displayed, not just the icon, I can personally approve this PR.

For example, if an issue is reported, a screenshot showing only the error icon is not helpful. It requires extra effort to tell the user to click the icon to view the error. Instead, it would be better to have a scrollable container that always displays one line of the error text if errors are detected, so the user can immediately see that many lines of the error are contained within that container and understand that they simply need to copy it. In other words, the most important thing is to be able to list all the reasons why the AnimationTree isn't working, regardless of the scope.

I understand, I'd like to offer my counterpoint one last time.

As the AnimationTree is built, the user will naturally become intimated as to why certain things aren't working, which they can resolve as they crop up. They are practically guaranteed to see errors as they build their tree, and with most solutions being very straightforward: a limited scope trains users to resolve these on-site. Additionally, there already is knowledge from the Script Editor to rely on for awareness of the button.

Also, the AnimationTree does work, with errors present. I have a lot of parallel unused BlendTree chains that I keep as backups of alternative flows, it serves me no purpose to have a line of red text always in my vision. In my opinion, any sufficiently complex project would too: have something they must keep in a Tree and would rather be ignored. Isn't it going too far to have the elegance of day-to-day UI be sacrificed in service of edge cases? This is my vested interest that I was representing when I said "intrusive" in my original issue.

Before the optimisation PR, the error panel used to only show the current plugin scope, was it an intentional change to this? Would it be possible ask for consensus at the next meeting, if there's one before feature freeze?

This was not intentional, but to begin with, instance safety was not adequately ensured before the optimization. After the optimization, this is more of a side effect resulting from instances now being passed via arguments. Before the optimization, this propagation simply wasn’t working properly.

> Also, the AnimationTree does work, with errors present. I have a lot of parallel unused BlendTree chains that I keep as backups of alternative flows, it serves me no purpose to have a line of red text always in my vision. In my opinion, any sufficiently complex project would too: have something they must keep in a Tree and would rather be ignored. Isn't it going too far to have the elegance of day-to-day UI be sacrificed in service of edge cases? This is my vested interest that I was representing when I said "intrusive" in my original issue.

If an error within a specific nested level does not stop the entire AnimationTree, it makes sense to display the error only within that nested level. However, if that nested layer is the playback target and the AnimationTree’s output is being blocked, that error must definitely be displayed in the AnimationTree Editor at least one line.

Rather than a situation where it’s not clear that an error has actually occurred such as when playback is blocked but only an error icon is displayed, we should prioritize a clear indication that an error has occurred such as displaying at least one line of error text and showing a scrollable container. So, we should prioritize clear error notifications even if they’re a bit intrusive, rather than insufficient error notifications in cases where they’re truly necessary simply due to a lack of distinction.

In other words, if you want to ignore errors that do not affect playback, I believe we need to distinguish between "whether the AnimationTree's output is blocked and animations are currently unable to play" and other cases. I think the handling of this "invalid" flag changed before and after the optimization, but we should be able to make some distinction there. If feasible, you could send it as a follow-up PR.

Is "Error ![StatusError](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c397d263-0cc2-4696-9c65-72604bb19700)" vs "Warning ![NodeWarning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3aa5f3e3-f985-46d3-b9b7-640e77e89d68)" a suitable semantic? One would block animation flow eventually, the other can not. The former is shown persistently (preferring scope when selecting which one), while warnings are only ever in their dedicated button, like in Script Editor.

Could also be "Unlinked ![Unlinked](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cd2f702-1c65-441b-bae8-4c232790ee5c)" instead, to note strays in both StateMachine and BlendTree with less severity.

For example, if there is an unconnected BlendTree within a StateMachine (this StateMachine is RootBlendTree) and it is in a state where it will never be played, it makes sense for an invalid state within the BlendTree to be treated as a warning. However, if it is connected to a State (or just selected to playback it) and is in a state where blending for playback actually occurs, it should be treated as an error and at least one line of text should be displayed as an error message in all relevant locations on the AnimationTreeEditor. If you can making that distinction is possible, it would be fine to implement it.

Got it, I will save it for a follow up.

Squashed, an error if available is always shown. The priority for selection is:
1. Direct scope (current node or non-editable child).
2. Downstream (editable child or deeper).
3. First error from tally.

That being said, it does have a paradigm I admire, that clicking on the error gives an explanation for that error. If the first click was to take the user to the error, and if they were already at the site, the second offered an explanation popup, that could be good.

> i.e., whether BlendSpace is active, meaning whether the weight of BlendSpace itself is non-zero

Not sure what you mean by this... if the offending BlendSpace is the currently open node, the error is visible as the current error on the persistent label, same as in #117275. It is also visible in the log.

The priority now for the persistent label now is:
1. Error reported by current node's editor plugin (sync in BlendSpace & playback in StateMachine)
2. Direct scope (current node or non-editable child).
3. Downstream (editable child or deeper).
4. First error in log.

I also changed `KeyInvalid`'s svg to be 10px (up from 8px), like `KeyValue` and `KeySelected`, because it wasn't centered otherwise.

Migration is complete, I'd like save further improvements like infoboxes to help the user each issue, as well as a flash when jumping to a new node via an error's click function for follow ups.

Right, so it should be reported by the BlendSpace node's `add_validation_error` instead, not the editor plugin.
The distinction between warnings and errors should be saved for a follow up, like I said, but thank you for letting me know where to look when that happens.

Admittedly, the current situation where errors are detected separately in the editor and in the actual AnimationNode is a problem. I believe that whether or not an error exists should be reported by the AnimationNode itself.

However, it may be inconvenient that the node cannot determine if its own setup is actually in error until the AnimationTree becomes active and the process is executed. I think this is one reason why errors are currently being detected on the editor side.

It would be possible to detect errors by running the process in a test mode whenever a resource is modified, but in any case, that would involve a minor refactoring.

> It would be possible to detect errors by running the process in a test mode whenever a resource is modified, but in any case, that would involve a minor refactoring.

I see. For the most part, however, this PR does decouple the error from the individual editors at least, so whenever that does happen it should be easier. Regarding the StateMachine playback error, I'm not sure how to meet its conditions. Were you able to test that it's working?

Thank you for the approval, but before merge: let me investigate if the BlendSpace cyclic invalidity error can be migrated from the editor to the node.

> Regarding the StateMachine playback error, I'm not sure how to meet its conditions. Were you able to test that it's working? I don’t think this error occurs under normal usage. This is because the Playback object is a read-only property that is created and assigned every frame. I seem to recall that this error may have been introduced in the past to detect an unintended bug that allowed any Playback object to be assigned, but it might simply be a remnant from version 3.x. So I think you don't need to worry about it too much. > but before merge: let me investigate if the BlendSpace cyclic invalidity error can be migrated from the editor to the node. If it’s not that serious, you can send it as a follow-up since the feature freeze is close.
Ready to merge, in that case.
Thanks!
